newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM not optimistic over Peru hostage crisis.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM not optimistic over Peru hostage crisis.

text.p: Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Friday he did not foresee dramatic progress soon in talks between the Peruvian government and Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima.
"I can't say with confidence that there will be significant progress," Hashimoto told reporters.
"I am not optimistic," he said without elaborating.

In Peru on Thursday, one hundred days after Marxist rebels stormed the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima taking hundreds of hostages, there was a sense of optimism that a negotiated solution may be in sight.
Even Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori's opponents in Congress saw a quick end to the crisis.
"The way negotiations are progressing, I believe they can come up with a solution in the short term," Congressman Alejandro Santa Maria Silva of the Aprista party told Reuters.

The wave of optimism among diplomats and politicians this week was reinforced on Thursday by comments from Fujimori and the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels who are holding 72 hostages at the residence in plush San Isidro.
"Even though, naturally, difficulties still exist, we are getting closer," Fujimori told a television interviewer.

An MRTA military leader in Peru's central jungle agreed there was progress but said the government still had to come up with a satisfactory offer to meet the rebels' demand for the freedom of jailed comrades. "The sides are getting closer but the main demand for the release of prisoners still has to be addressed," Comrade Alejandro told Reuters from the jungle.

Diplomats, legislators and analysts all say that, although they foresee tough discussions on how many, if any, of the 450 MRTA imprisoned rebels would be released, that should not become an unsurmountable hurdle when face-to-face contacts resume, presumably early next week after the Easter holiday.
